title: Guardian technology
scope: GKI-02 catalogue: every Guardian Technology Broker offering documented on the reviewed pages (23 permanent unlocks: 6 modules, 14 weapon variants, 3 ship-launched fighters; 6 per-item purchases of modified weapons), their exact recipes, the materials and commodities they consume, Guardian blueprint, beacon and obelisk sites, and the activities that supply each requirement. Human broker items, Thargoid and lore records are out of scope.
game_version: No source ties these facts to a specific current game version. Technology Brokers arrived in 3.0 (2018-02-27); the Guardian fighters in 3.2; the booster was re-released in 3.1. Reviewed against page revisions current on 2026-10-29.
rights_basis: Original OmniCOVAS records of Elite Dangerous game facts: requirements, quantities, identifiers, system, body and station names, distances, module statistics and procedures, written in OmniCOVAS's own words. The facts were researched from the cited community references, which are credited per claim. No wiki prose, tables, images, in-game description text or third-party code is reproduced; a word-sequence comparison against every cited page revision found no shared run longer than five words outside proper names (GKI-01 distribution record). Frontier game assets are not included.

distribution.basis: Content audit for GKI-01 (2026-10-29) and the GKI-02 catalogue extension (2026-10-29): every record is an original OmniCOVAS statement of game facts or OmniCOVAS-authored metadata; the extension was checked with the curator expression check before release.

entities.name: Guardian FSD Booster unlock
entities.summary: A one-time hand-in at a Guardian Technology Broker that permanently adds the Guardian Frame Shift Drive Booster to Outfitting at Guardian broker stations.

claims.text: The hand-in is made once. Afterwards each booster is bought with credits in Outfitting, with no further materials.
Every requested item must be handed in together; the broker does not take instalments.
Technology Broker services require Horizons content.
After unlocking, the booster can be bought at any station with a Guardian Technology Broker.
The game writes a TechnologyBroker Journal event when an unlock is used, listing the unlocked items and the resources consumed.

entities.name: Guardian Frame Shift Drive Booster
entities.summary: Optional internal module of Guardian origin that adds a flat bonus to the ship's frame shift drive jump range.

attributes.summary_line: Optional internal, classes 1 to 5, rating H: +4.0 to +10.5 ly jump range

claims.text: Adds a fixed number of light years to jump range: 4.0, 6.0, 7.75, 9.25 or 10.5 ly for classes 1 to 5.
Listed base values run from 405,020 CR (class 1) to 6,483,100 CR (class 5). Station prices can differ.
The module cannot be engineered.
Journal module symbols are Int_GuardianFSDBooster_Size1 to Size5.
First released in April 2018, withdrawn within hours, and re-released in update 3.1 on 2018-06-28 with a revised jump bonus.

entities.name: Small Guardian Structure
entities.summary: Small Guardian ruin layout defended by sentinels. Its Ancient Data Terminal needs a Guardian Relic and gives module or weapon blueprint segments, depending on the site.

claims.text: Small structures hold module or weapon blueprint terminals; large structures (located through Guardian Beacons) hold vessel blueprints and need an Ancient Key instead.
Structures show in the navigation panel once you are within about 1,000 ls of them.
Expect at least six sentinels at a small site: three while raising pylons, one when all are charged and two after the terminal opens.

entities.name: Activate a module-blueprint data terminal
entities.summary: Power a Guardian site's six pylons with an SRV, open the terminal with a relic and scan its core for one blueprint segment.

attributes.yields: one blueprint segment per commander per activation

steps.text: Land beside the structure and deploy the SRV.
Drive up to the terminal to raise its two adjacent pylons. They must rise before any others.
Drive to the four remaining pylons around the site to raise them, dealing with sentinels as they appear.
Shoot each pylon's glowing core to charge it. The first hit starts a timer, and all six must be fully charged before it runs out. SRV plasma or ship weapons both work.

With all six charged, drop the site's key item from the SRV's cargo into the lit socket before the terminal: a Guardian Relic at small structures, an Ancient Key at large ones. Further sentinels then arrive.
Scan the raised data core with the SRV data link scanner to receive one blueprint segment of the site's kind: module, weapon or vessel.
In a wing, every commander scans for their own segment; the terminal can be re-powered between scans.
To repeat the same site yourself, log out and back in first. A second scan without relogging gives nothing.

claims.text: Module and weapon terminals need a Guardian Relic; vessel terminals need an Ancient Key.

entities.name: Activate a weapon-blueprint data terminal
entities.summary: Same terminal procedure as for module blueprints, at the small Guardian structures whose terminal holds weapon schematics.

attributes.yields: one weapon blueprint segment per commander per activation

claims.text: These terminals also need a Guardian Relic placed before the core can be scanned.
Weapon-blueprint sites are different structures from module-blueprint sites.

entities.name: Activate a vessel-blueprint data terminal
entities.summary: Terminal procedure at a large Guardian structure found through a beacon; the terminal opens with an Ancient Key instead of a relic.

attributes.yields: one vessel blueprint segment per commander per activation

claims.text: Large structures open their terminal with an Ancient Key, not a Guardian Relic.
Large structures are guarded by up to twelve sentinels at once.
Re-scanning the same structure without relogging gives nothing, which can mean another trip to the beacon for a new key.

entities.name: Reactivate a Guardian Beacon
entities.summary: Charge an orbital beacon's three pylons with ship weapons, then scan its core to receive an Ancient Key.

steps.text: Fly to the beacon, an orbital Guardian structure in space.
Shoot the charging point of any of its three energy pylons; from that moment you have three minutes to charge the remaining two.
Scan the exposed data core with a data link scanner.
Collect the Ancient Key the beacon releases. Repeat the reactivation for more keys.

claims.text: Each beacon points to one large Guardian structure with a vessel-blueprint terminal.

entities.name: Destroy Guardian Sentinels
entities.summary: Destroy the sentinels that defend Guardian structures and collect what they drop.

claims.text: Destroyed sentinels drop Guardian Sentinel Weapon Parts and Wreckage Components.
Sentinels fire burst energy cannons and homing energy missiles; point defence can shoot the missiles down.

entities.name: Collect Guardian structure materials
entities.summary: Pick up the Guardian materials recovered around a Guardian structure site.

claims.text: Guardian Power Conduits are recovered at Guardian structure sites.

entities.name: Scan Guardian obelisks
entities.summary: Scan active obelisks from an SRV to capture encoded obelisk data in one of five patterns.

steps.text: Drive the SRV up to an obelisk group; at least one obelisk usually lights up and shows moving symbols.
Target the lit face and scan it using the data link scanner on your SRV to receive one data package.
A scanned obelisk stays inactive until your next login.

claims.text: Five data patterns exist, named Alpha to Epsilon.
Obelisks stand at Ancient Ruins and at Guardian structures.

entities.name: Surface prospecting
entities.summary: Collect raw materials from outcrops and meteorite types on planet surfaces using the SRV.

steps.text: Choose a landable body. A Detailed Surface Scanner map lists the raw materials it can yield; anything not listed never appears there.
Land and deploy an SRV. The ship needs a Planetary Vehicle Hangar, and the vehicle is bought separately.
Find outcrops and meteorites with the SRV's wave scanner and break them with SRV or ship weapons.
Scoop the chunks; each outcrop chunk gives three units of its material.

claims.text: Most raw materials, including the six Guardian recipes use, are found by surface prospecting.
Each body can yield eleven raw materials: one rare, two standard, three common and five very common, which are always Carbon, Iron, Nickel, Phosphorus and Sulphur.
Lead and Rhenium never come from planet surfaces; they are found only by asteroid mining.
Storage per material is capped by grade: 300, 250, 200, 150 and 100 for grades 1 to 5.

entities.name: Asteroid mining
entities.summary: Raw materials can be collected while mining asteroids.

steps.text: Fit a mining laser and fly to an asteroid field or planetary ring.
Fire the laser at an asteroid to cut fragments from its surface.
Collect the fragments with the cargo scoop or collector limpets. A refinery is needed only to turn fragments into commodities.

claims.text: Chromium, Carbon, Niobium, Arsenic and Germanium are listed as obtainable by asteroid mining.
Asteroid mining is a documented raw material source, and the only one for Lead and Rhenium.
Collector limpets do not tell legal from stolen containers; take care collecting near other ships.

entities.name: Signal sources in Boom systems
entities.summary: Investigate signal sources in systems in a Boom state for manufactured salvage.

steps.text: Find a system in a Boom state; signal source contents depend on allegiance, state, security and where in the system you are.
Target a signal source in supercruise to read its type and threat level (0 to 9), drop in and scoop the salvage before it expires.

claims.text: A listed source of Phase Alloys.

entities.name: Salvage from trading ships
entities.summary: Collect material drops from destroyed trading-role ships.

steps.text: Transport and trading ships fly the shipping lanes and appear in signal sources.
Scoop what they drop when destroyed; larger ships tend to drop the higher grades.

claims.text: The listed source of Heat Resistant Ceramics.
